To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in adult hearts, the sinoatrial (pacemaker) node area has the highest ratio of muscarinic (parasympathetic) receptor to beta-AR (sympathetic) mRNA, while in the aged heart, this ratio is similar to that of the surrounding myocardium, and this change is associated with a fragmentation and loss of acetylcholine esterase staining in the SA node.
the sinoatrial pacemaker of the senesced heart is less responsive to adrenergic stimulation and more responsive to cholinergic stimulation compared to the sinoatrial of the adult heart.
in senescent rat heart there is a change in the expression of beta-adrenergic and cholinergic receptor genes that affects the sinoatrial region of the right atrium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of molecular mechanisms involved in heart rate variability in the aging rat heart.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the age-associated modifications in the cardiac pacemaker.
a new mechanism of age-associated changes in the heart.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the age-associated change in the M2/beta-AR ratio in the SA node area is a specific change that occurs in senescence and not in adulthood, and that this change is not associated with a change in the M1/M2 ratio.
the senescent sinoatrial node is less responsive to the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems.

the senescent myocardium has a decreased ability to adapt its adrenergics-muscarinics receptor profile in the sinoatria area, a phenomenon that may contribute to the age-related impairment of heart rate variability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the adult heart, the sinoatrial region has a higher proportion of M2-R mRNA relative to β-AR mRNA, whereas the ratio of these two types of mRNA is similar in senescent hearts.
in adult hearts, beta1-AR mRNA levels are higher within the sinoatrials than in adjacent myocardium, while beta2-AR and M3-R mRNA levels are lower in sinoatrial than in atrium.
the senescent sinoatrial node is characterized by a decrease of M2-R/betAR mRNA ratio and a fragmentation of acetycholinesterase.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sinoatrial (SAN) node, the pacemaker area of the heart, is a heterogeneous region, and that the expression of genes involved in heart rate variability changes specifically within the SAN area of aged animals.
the senescent rat heart is characterized by an alteration of the adrenergic/muscarinic phenotype within the SA node.
the sinoatrial region is a specific target of aging, and this may be a key factor to understand the mechanisms responsible for the age-related modifications of heart rate variability.
